title: Good but needs improvement.
body: I have used several different GPS apps and found that I gravitate toward copilot. Your product overall is good here comes the but, it needs CarPlay feature. This would elevate your product substantially.

title: Intentionally limited potential
body: I honestly love this app, and I hope I can change my rating tom5 stars, but there’s some changes I’d need to see first. 1. Split View support for iPads - after being on the fence, I bought an ipad for my business to use over a cell phone as I saw the update log said Split View was now supported. It isn’t. When I contacted support, they said that was an error, that Split View support is built in, but only available to “enterprise customers”. Aka companies that pay a lot more. I can understand limiting some features to enterprise customers, but Split View is a very basic feature at this point, and is honestly a near necessity to have when competing. Additionally, to use this app you must pay for a license, meaning I’m paying for a license to use an app that locks out basic key features without option to even pay $5-10 more for certain features 2. Satellite view - I understand it would take more licensing, however I feel like satellite view is another major feature copilot loses out on. Without 1&2, I feel like I’m better off going with a certain competitor, unlike copilot, they do not show exit numbers and their road names data is outdated and often inaccurate. Copilot has had some of the most accurate map data I’ve used in terms of trucking gps, and I highly prefer copilot for Oversize load permits. 3. Speed limits - there is a option in settings to show speed Iimits, and to have alerts when speeding, however despite turning these features on, I have never once been shown a speed limit, nor shown my speed or alerted that im speeding. Not sure if this feature is meant to work at all Really hope these features are added/fixed.

title: Needs Work
body: Downloaded the truck trial form use with my RV. I used it in conjunction with my Garmin RV 795. The Co-pilot app didn’t try and take me under low over passes but it did try and send me down primitive roads. The Garmin did a much better job. I was hoping for a good car play option but this isn’t it.

title: Bugs out a lot
body: The routing is solid, and the shape route feature is very important for any commercial GPS, unfortunately certain features predictively and constantly bug the software, such as the “avoid this road” feature, if you use that in a trip at all, it will completely break the trip, and you will lose access to any of the shaping features, forcing you to clear the trip and rebuild your route. Heads up traffic breaks a lot, the bar will randomly disappear all together, and the device will get locked in on false road closure reports, messing up the predictive ETA and causing the routing to be useless until past whatever falsified closure reports. And it seems with the online routing edition, they are moving away from the route shaping features that caused this product to stand out in the first place.

title: Please add CarPlay
body: This app is ok. Especially if you have no service. It lacks CarPlay. That kills a higher rating.

title: Issue with Arrived Destination Notice
body: After recent updates, arrived at destination notification pops up way too early. Meaning I still needs to make 3 more turns with least 100 yard to go, Arrived notification pops up and can’t see the map. Please fix the arrived notifications timing to which it actually arrived to destination.

title: When it works it has some nice features BUT
body: As I said, nice features for adding several stops but doesn’t always recognize them. Also, downloaded the US map as this is where we live. Didn’t expect to have to do it again when we returned from Canada BUT had to. Even after that, it thought we were still in Canada and didn’t recognize US destinations. Frustrating and dangerous because of the unreliability when you need directions at your fingertips.

title: Long haul trucker review
body: The good: it’s got a feature called “avoid this road” The bad: that feature works about 50% of the time, and after numerous back and forth emails with support, I’ve determined that the only way to avoid a road reliably is to make numerous waypoints. Very annoying. The good: fairly intuitive user interface The bad: horrendous voice options for turn-by-turn navigation. I had to close the female New Zealander voice because it was the least grating. And it’s not great. The good: it’s pretty decent in terms of routing on major highways. The bad: it is utterly horrendous on smaller highways and streets. Almost every time I get into a smaller town or out into the country, it attempts to route my 40 ton, 70+ foot long vehicle down residential streets far too narrow for a truck, often with power lines and/or tree limbs that are too low for my 13’ 6” clearance, or straight up have signs restricting trucks. When I say almost every time, I mean, literally I have to approach EVERY turn in these kinds of areas with immense caution as the likelihood of getting into a situation if I follow the gps is exceptionally high. OVERALL: I used to pay for a subscription to this app. After all the issues, I decided to cough up the money for a dedicated truck gps. They all have their issues, none are perfect. But my Garmin was far superior in that at least it almost never routed me illegally. Then my company purchased a mass subscription for anyone in the company who wanted it. I figured that if large companies are infusing the developers with cash, then it’s probably well improved since I quit using it. Now, I’ve realized that my company is just giving people who can’t afford a truck gps an option that is at least better than Google maps for a truck. I’m not happy with this product. It’s marginally useful. I sincerely hope they start paying closer attention to the issues thousands of people have been complaining about.

title: Still no Apple CarPlay
body: Every car, RV, and truck offers in vehicle Apple CarPlay but still not supported.

title: Not following Mile On app PC Miler
body: My complain is that CO Pilot does not follow the route provided by the mile on app…. I have the mile on app setting for shortest route…. Once it transfers to Navigate to CoPilot it restructures the whole trip to a more practical route but with more miles…

title: Good routing, poor database
body: The routing is great and does just what it promises. However, an app built for RVers ought to have campgrounds loaded in its database. We typically don’t know the address of the campground we are heading to next. All other GPS I have used had campgrounds and other points of interest loaded in its database. Add those and this would be a 6 / 5 stars app.

title: No way to report an error
body: I routed to the Saint Mary Montana KOA using their street address and it took me to a meadow on US 89 about 8 miles away. I had to use Apple maps to get ti the KOA. I'm sure the KOA store has truck deliveries at least once a week.

title: Nice app to have around
body: Inexpensive gps app that’s nice to have. I’ve encounter situation where cellular reception didn’t work and had to rely on copilot to find where I’m going. Or when you don’t have unlimited cellular data and had to do long distance driving, so it’s nice to have an app with the maps downloaded locally. Recently took a trip to LA to visit friend, who lives in a newly built community within 1 year. Unfortunate the copilot map does not have the updates so could set an destination address.

title: Average
body: I’ve been using this GPS app for awhile until the system failed. Had a subscription for a year. Somehow I was asked to purchase again in order to use. I canceled the subscription right away. Now I got back at it again, spend 15 minutes trying to create a new account, but non o of my three emails and different types of passwords worked. Kept saying “failed failed failed…”. I guess there are bunch of errors now that it wasn’t before. Otherwise this is not bad GPS for a truck. I was pretty happy using it.

title: Ok !!
body: Needs to work with apple car play. Has given me bad directions a few times putting us on small gravel roads with very sharp turns. Also loses gps signal often. Will not pay for another year.

title: Good idea, issues with routing
body: I liked the of real-time RV routing without selling my soul to good Sam but after using for two weeks on a long RV trip I have some issues with the routing. Going through several major cities on I40 it consistently wanted to rout via bypasses even though the straight through routes were faster. It also has a tendency to take you off interstates for short stretches on secondary roads and then put you back on the same interstate. This makes no sense for RV routing. I find my self having to check the copilot routing against google maps to make sure it doesn’t do anything stupid. After completing a 50 day cross county Rv trip I still have lots of issues with the routing. In several cases we were routed on small gravel roads totally unsuited for an RV. Looks like I’ll need to look for an alternate solution

title: Speed Limit is broken?
body: The GPS UI won’t show the Speed Limit. Otherwise, love the app on my phone for truck. Would update the review once it’s fixed.

title: Traffic update lags
body: I am a truck driver assigned to east coast run. My route stays the same (pick up and drop offs) however my window of delivery is super tight as my day’s success or failure is determined in minutes not hours. I use Co Pilot because the routing is almost good balance of practical route vs traffic avoidance. I can work with the balance issue how my number 1 complaint with the app is that the traffic eta takes a few mins to update. Often the app will suggest a faster route but that is without the updated traffic data that is often worst then following the original traffic route.

title: Not optimized for iPads
body: The UI is not optimized for the larger screens on iPads. Too zoomed in.

title: Good app but…
body: I like the features as they are easy to navigate through and switch from one view to another. I would purchase CoPilot but will not as it is not compatible with Apple Car Play at this time. This is the reason for the 3 stars

title: Wrong time
body: Every time I set my destination before I hit my trip “example”it’ll say 3 hours 38 minutes then when I start my trip it’ll jump from 3 hours 38 minutes to 4 hours 58 minutes,it has been dong this for about a year now!!

title: Works great but…
body: Great app to use when you’re a commercial driver but even after you subscribe it keeps asking you to subscribe. And gives you only 10 days from that point. If you rely on the app for work then it’s a real inconvenience trying to get it to remember the subscription. I hope tech-support reads this and fixes the bug.

title: Good that map data is local but…
body: I like that the map data is stored on my phone so no cell service is required to use but this app is not very intuitive. I find it difficult to navigate the various options. In addition, I cannot search for some exact street addresses (I can on other apps).

title: Pretty good
body: It keeps me from going under low underpasses and works well for that most of the time. It’s clunky and sounds terrible and some addresses it can’t find. And the find an address thing is weird that you have to put in the city first and then the address it’s just not smooth and easy like Google maps or Apple Maps I would expect that if I’m paying all this money.

title: Maps
body: Unable to download maps. Sits there forever anot downloading. This prevents me from opening the app until it’s downloaded.

title: Update Broke 3D Split View Turn Directions
body: Latest Update Broke 3D Split View Turn Directions. Please Fix ASAP! They show up for a split second and then disappear??.. Other than that Best Truck GPS by far! I’ll change my review to 5 Stars once fixed (just hope to get your attention). Also wish my subscription allowed for more than one device. It would help with trip planning to be able to use at least one other device. Thank you

title: App mishaps
body: I rate it a 3 only because of the RV specifications not being correct. The RV height input Specifically. I had problems getting it to allow the inch data to be input. Email response was ok the 1st time subsequently the 2nd request was not answered for 4 days. Hopefully the update will be fixed ASAP.

title: Help
body: I have download this app to both my iPad and iPhone. It works great on my iPhone but the gps doesn’t work with my iPad I’ve went through all the settings on the app and my iPad and sill won’t work please help

title: What happened
body: I used to be a real supporter of CoPilot but after buying the “RV” version, I’ve become disappointed. Yesterday we drove from Niagara Falls to Cooperstown, a trip your software claimed was 4.75 hours, turned into a 7 hour nightmare! Twice we were directed to a 2 lane road and across a 2ton capacity bridge in a vehicle weighing 32000 lbs. it wanted us to turn left onto a one lane dirt road. I checked the settings on the software and the size and weight of our RV were set. Sure would like to see the track of our trip to Cooperstown NY. Can I get my money back?

title: Nice RV Nav
body: Navigation works great. It uses a voice similar to a really old Garmin that’s very robotic sounding. My only real complaint is that the static bars around the screen for traffic and other information caused my iPhone 12 Pro to have the images burned into the display. I’m currently trying different things to fix my screen.

title: OTR Use: iPas & iPhone
body: Use the application w/ iOS. The basic functionality is good; however, being able to export trips would be helpful. Also, speed limits need to be updated.

title: Heads up view all mixed up
body: The app seems to have a mind of its own with heads up vs north up view, and often displays a lopsided view. This is very disorienting! Also, the font size for the speed - altitude - distance displays aresmall and pencil thin. It needs to be bigger and in bold face.

title: Not good!
body: I've unfortunately been using this app for three years because when they update the app I feel like it gets better before it gets worse. I don't know why I'm paying ten bucks a month for this app. The roads don't update very often and the app will try to take me down cemetery roads and non existent roads. It also constantly tries to bring me down one way streets and no truck roads. If your going to use this app you have to constantly look at your phone to make sure it's not screwing you into a ticket. On top of all this the app will randomly freeze and you'll have to restart it. Most times you don't realize it froze until you've gone way past your turn. Find another truck gps app!

title: Needs Car Play support
body: I love the app but you need to add car play for Apple and the same for android. My RV has a 10 inch screen and I would love to be using Car Play to see the map.

title: CarPlay
body: Add this to CarPlay more trucks are coming with Apple CarPlay I have a CarPlay enabled stereo Would make use of gps very convenient

title: Missing CarPlay
body: Copilot is a good offline GPS app, but missing CarPlay makes it less desirable. CarPlay would make it it much safer than using you iPhone while driving.

title: Needs work
body: Im curious if yall are getting any feedback from actual truck drivers? The app is kind of clunky needs more dashboard features. Kind of difficult to look for truck stops or rest areas up ahead. Will be trying the hazmat features, will report back

title: CarPlay
body: I gave only 3 stars for one reason. Luck of CarPlay. When it will become available I will increase it.

title: No license after update
body: I searched for a route and explored poi’s along the route today. . Then decided to run the update. When I opened it, I was presented with the sign up screen and asked to renew my license. I’m not sure when I purchased the license; but I’m pretty sure it wasn’t in the middle of today. How do I confirm date of purchase and get license reset?

title: Somewhat Disappointing
body: Just downloaded this app, paid my annual fee, and started using. I guess I was expecting WAZE like performance but with the ability to enter my vehicle type and size for avoiding obstacles. What I got instead was Garmin like rote planning (not terribly intuitive) with the ability to enter vehicle info. My biggest gripe so far, it can’t find locations I want to go to. My motorhome uses diesel fuel, and I’m part of a purchase program through Love’s Travel Stops. Co-Pilot cannot find a single Love’s Travel Stop. I have to lookup the address, then enter it directly. Even then it found the wrong location. Eventually I discovered how to pick the waypoint on the map and enter it as a stop. In summary, I find this tool to be precarious at best. It is riddled with 2001 technology and gps mapping concepts. As I use and grow with it, I will come back and update this review, but for now. . . I’m unimpressed with it, and less than thrilled.

title: HaZmat
body: I do not on this app just yet but I would like to know without paying for it does it offer hazmat trucking routes?

title: Love it
body: Love this app but can’t get My active traffic to work. Use it all the time. Would be a 5 if I could. Paid for it but no result.

title: No CarPlay?
body: For a navigation app that charges money to not support CarPlay and Android Auto it’s a little disappointing.

title: The app
body: Problem with download, freezing, and sometimes gives inaccurate information on directions near areas that have low cellular activity. Assuming data flow is the issue but it could just be the app workflow. I dunno

title: Ok but sometimes freezes
body: App is great for RV on small Cornish lanes, however the maps on screen aren’t as clear as something like Google maps for guidance and on major roads it sometimes rerouted much longer ways than was necessary. It would also sometimes freeze mid journey requiring a restart. It did the job for my RV holiday but I won’t buy it.

title: CarPlay?
body: 5 star app when it’s compatible with CarPlay

title: Had to downgrade
body: I normally don’t reviews, but in this scenario it’s must for your benefit. This version of the app added an auto renew features, which broke the app, made it completely unusable, because it won’t let us pay for the service. I actually enjoy using this gps service while I’m driving my semi. The solution for me was to downgrade my app to the last version, which was a pain, but it solved the issue. Now Customers love convenience and ease of use, forcing customers to message support to active service is basically shooting yourself in the foot. Creating an avoidable inconvenience and making it difficult for customers to pay just isn’t financially logical. Just downgrade the app from the market till you’re able to resolve this bug.

title: Updates seem to be making the app glitchy.
body: Have been using the app for years, but recent updates have been making the app worse. They’ve taken out the option to choose preferred roads and now, after the latest update, I have to boot the app a few times before it remembers I’ve paid for the month ... which alone is annoying that they can’t just use Apple’s subscription service to automatically renew. Most subscription based apps seem to be able to do this without glitches. Hopefully they can fix the problems.

title: Not able to subs
body: App is okay, except it has some faults like queensboro bridge in Queens, its takes u to a path where trucks are forbidden. The problem i has is that I subsrcribed for one month but now after it expired i try to extend, but whenever i hit renew it takes me to a page with the prices, i select the same option i has before(which expired) and nothing happens.

title: Why can’t I renew
body: After trial have been trying to renew through the app for days and it keeps freezing. Have deleted and reinstalled multiple times. So frustrating I ended up deleting the app.

title: Like it
body: I like it but it won’t let me renew

title: Car Play
body: Looks like something I would pay money for if it only interfaced with Apple Car Play. I need to get away from using a stand alone RV GPS.

title: Stopped letting me renew..
body: I used this app everyday for work as I am a truck driver, never had any issues as I always double confirmed my routes with a map beforehand but as of the last month or so it will no longer allow me to renew it, so now I have no reliable truck gps on my phone. Super irritating. This was the much cheaper option over buying a 4-500 standalone unit. Please fix your app.

title: The app would be 5 star with Car Play support
body: The app does a really good job taking into account rig size and routing away from low clearances. It would be fantastic if the app supported Car Play so one would only have the in dash display to check while under way.

title: Rv option
body: Why don’t the app I have for rv . Please advise !

title: Disappointed
body: Had read some good reviews but in general have been disappointed with the interface of the app and poor location choices for searches over months we have had the app. St Augustine Florida does not populate as a search choice, for example, (either when trying to plan a route from New England. Any “web” search is just a yelp handcuff. The routing has been good through the tricky parts of CT, NJ and NY pikes, but that is not enough to overcome the inability to give a reasonable destination for initial route planning or when changing a destination on the fly. It would have warranted 4 stars if it were a lower cost subscription or was free. Not likely to renew the subscription.

title: Ok not great
body: This is OK but not great. Very good at choosing truck routes away from major highways. Once it chooses a route, it will not adapt to a new route. It will only choose a U-turn to go to the original route. Must have another map app running until this one catches up. Way to much ramp directions & not enough direction after ramp. Exit numbers are not consistently provided. Gives street names but not highway numbers.

title: About the same as other Nav apps
body: Used this for the 14 day trial after reading an RV forum that recommended it for full time RVers. Found it nice to use for the turn. I turn features and thought it great you could put in trailer dimensions etc. however it didn’t route any differently than Google Maps in most areas and it took us down some difficult to navigate side streets just like google did instead of on larger highways that would have been better for trailering. Will not spend money on it.

title: Password reset
body: I try to reset my password but didn’t receive any email

title: Was trying it out!!!
body: Trying the free trial to test it out!!! App is freezing but still giving me directions. I have closed out app and rebooted my phone!!

title: Not bad
body: Over all its good. Only issues really annoying is when you pick a route and instead of stick with it gos trying to all the time take you through some kind of highways just to bring you to same interstate 10 miles down the road. Or it keeps wanting for you to take exit just so you can go back right on interstate. Some of the routes its splits for example instead of just keep i95 to go to fl it keeps wanting to take 95 then bunch of different highways just so you can get back to i 95 later traffic alert not that great at all and when they doing construction it tells you that interstate is closed completely and trying to reroute you

title: IOS 13.2 lost voice navigation
body: So far copilot was good, but on new ios 13.2 app lost voice navigation :(

title: Appdate GPS
body: The updates are excellent—thanks, and keep up the good work. There is just one thing missing: you could mention the cities. You might not need to name the freeway itself, but please mention the cities the driver is heading toward.

title: CarPlay
body: Finally! I’ve been waiting for the CarPlay connectivity for quite some time so I do appreciate the addition of the feature to this update. However I have some constructive criticism; I notice in the info panel where it says your next turn out the exit that you get off the highway, the number is enshrouded with a green circle. Well that green circle makes it less visible. I would suggest just writing it in white color font as’Exit’ is written in.

title: Disappointing after using the Android version
body: I have had some version of Copilot since version 1 when it came on a disk for Windows. It’s always been regularly updated in the past with new features using the latest technology but this no longer seems to be the case on iOS. I’ve read the other reviews where they say we’re finally getting CarPlay support. I sorely hope we’re getting at least some of the many missing features I noticed when trying out Copilot on my friends Android device. It’s pretty telling when Hammer, a competitor that was free until just a couple of months ago and still costs half of what the truck version of Copilot does even now, has had those features and more for literally years. As much as I like this app, it’s severely out of date at this point and needs to get with the times.

title: Fantastic app, please add a compass.
body: This is a great app. It would be five stars if they had a compass. Please add a compass that can be activated/deactivated from the menu settings.

title: Thank you for improving compatibility with iOS 26.
body: Keep going. There’s more to do to make this work better in iOS 26.

title: Lifetime license
body: Well, copilot used to work in ios. After 20 plus years trimble map failed. Support was pretty good but they have no idea on how to fix their issues. Maybe a new verson might work. Not waiting to find out. Moved on to Sygic Maps. O Update. Many thanks to Michel, tech support. Working better. Side street rapds not working.

title: Great Navigation App
body: Copilot is the best navigation app I’ve found. I like the data being stored locally on the device since cellular access can often be limited on cross country trips. Lots of configurability. I would like to see the app store your route so it can be reviewed later. Also the navigation algorithm needs work as it often sends me on a less than efficient route. Sometimes it tells me to exit the freeway only to have get right back on.

title: Photo location input no working
body: The rating would be 5 stars if the app includes the photo location input and update map including info provided by users.

title: Support can help
body: I contacted support and the problem was fixed asap TY. I will update how the new maps are working.

title: Needs CarPlay
body: Love all the features of this Nav app. Can’t beat it for RVs or other vehicles that have unique travel restrictions or needs. Not having CarPlay integration though is very strange. When can we expect this? Please add this feature!

title: It keep crashing
body: My app keeps crashing every time I try to pull it up not sure what’s going on. Any answers to what to do thanks.

title: Updated review
body: I had originally submitted a one star review because of a feature I thought was not working…I feel a bit silly about how long it took me to figure it out (even with the help of support). Now that I have everything working, I’m glad to give it four stars. I would have given five, but the app often routes my stops out of order (I drive a bus and need to make stops in order). Also, I am frequently routed to approach one of my stops on the wrong side of the road. Otherwise, this app is one I’ve been looking for since starting this job, and I can work around the above mentioned concerns.

title: Tanks you now is working
body: Tanks

title: Obviously learn how to plan
body: This gps app has worked out so far. If you plan ahead and know where exactly you want to go with the right vehicle dimensions and restrictions added to settings, it will not mess you up. Learn how to plan before just putting an address and driving off because it might lead you down a road not intended for your vehicle, maybe because you didn’t specify what you are driving.

title: Good for RV
body: This is just about the only reliable navigation app for RVs. It’s no Google Maps, but it does route based on height/weight and keeps you on appropriate roads. The UI is quirky and takes getting used to. My biggest complaint…. Favorite locations don’t sync across devices without backing up to the cloud, logging out, and logging back in. Seems like that should be a basic feature.

title: Decent Maps
body: That is, if you don't want uncle Google to know all your places 🤭 Would like to see speed adjustment for spoken directions, as well as full screen display and distance in feet + miles, not yards. Other than that, I like it.

title: It’s a great app
body: I haul mobile homes and it helps being I don’t have a trucker’s gps. I only used it a few times but it’s a nice tool.

title: better than most
body: after using this app for more than 5 years for a class A RV up and down the astcoast and as far west as the Mississippi I am fairly confident about its routing- the one thing it needs to do corectly, it does: GPS routing. my feedback to the developers would be to include eta ( time and milage ) to next stop or waypoint while planning a trip ie see how far it is to a reststop/fuelstop/lunchstop.

title: Arrival time 😑
body: It hurts that I even have to give this review because I told so many drivers about how great of an app this is .. I don’t know what’s going on it gives you one time for example take 1 he and 15 minutes and then later you go back and it says 2 hours and that’s without it saying there’s traffic .. roads are clear but give one time and then another it’s frustrating especially when your boss is asking you what time your going to arrive and it tells you one hour but ends up two like I don’t get it .. wasn’t like that before and then you can’t even talk to anyone on here

title: PC Miler vs CoPilot
body: Being that both is owned by Trimble but mileage is different between the two systems. My company, using PC Miler, reduces my mileage by 200+/- miles each week. I use CoPilot ($120 a year). How can this be so far apart?? Killing my annual pay!

title: Works great … much better look than Garmin!
body: Love the look of the detailed maps on an iPad. We choose off the beaten path routes usually and when you do this the Garmin is out of it’s element. The confused Garmin thinks we are driving on someone’s lawn … doesn’t even show a road? One bug is when on “motorcycle” in settings, co-pilot sends you off the interstate and then back on the interstate for a two minute unneeded detour. Another is it fails to connect with the GPS at times, a power off/on usually fixes this. The look is something like a Tesla map which is top notch. So nice to have this, a happy user for the last 7-8 years!

title: Good trucking GPS
body: It’s better than Rand McNally that’s for sure Gets me where I need to go and has regular updates. Plus I don’t need to plug it into the computer. Sometimes you need to adjust your rout because it will try to take you the long way (it will take you up a major interstate when the backroads are shorter) but I thinks that’s any truck gps you get. Always double check your destination with google maps to ensure it’s taking you to the right place. It will get you to the correct street but not necessarily the dock. (Hence the 4 star review) You can drag and drop your destination pin once you have your rout/ address plugged in and you can place multiple pins if your load requires more than one stop. Would definitely recommend over stand alone units. Make sure you have your phone charger plugged in.

title: Ok
body: I’ve been using copilot for years. Currently the gps is trying to bring me down restricted roads and it never did that!

title: Great Navigation App
body: But it still needs to work. This will be the first and the best for Truck & others Navigation mobile app. Thank you for app.

title: Good app for RV routing
body: I’ve been using this app for a couple of years and for the most part it hasn’t let me down. Like all GPS apps, you should have a backup and an Over the Road trucker map to check the route that you’re going to take. I love being able to tell the app the road types I want to take. I’ve got a 40’ 5th wheel and being routed through an area with tight roads would be terrible. I tend to like to stick to bigger roads for less stress. Only issue I’ve found so far is that the max height is 13’ and my RV is 13’ 6”. Hopefully that will get corrected. Otherwise the app is solid. Again, make sure you have an over the road map available and check your route prior to heading out.

title: RV Navigation
body: I am still running on the trial. We are using it to go from Texas back to Michigan with 3 KOA stops. There isn’t any tricky routing issues on this trip but the trip planner was helpful in planning the trek home. Being able to pick from several possible routes is nice. The voice turn by turn has worked well and if we finally decide to subscribe we will add that feature. The issues that keep me from just clicking on the Buy Now buttonthe are the lack of CarPlay projection of the map and there isn’t a description of the next action until you are fairly close to needing to execute it. In an RV and dealing with heavy traffic sometimes the verbal description of the next action gets lost and having a set of symbols describing what to do next is extremely helpful. We did put the phone in a cup holder mount so that I could see the screen, but it is not in a convenient position to just glance at it. For this to really work I will need to figure out how to mount the phone next to the trailer’s RVC display in such a way that the sun coming in through the windshield doesn’t overheat it. One feature that would clinch the deal, but it doesn’t have, is a button to tell the app to stop navigating while we take a detour or just visit a rest area. Resuming the routing would have it recalculate where it is and update the routing. We do have Waze running at the same time to get the road conditions and to display the map on the dash. It isn’t doing any routing though

title: CoPilot Great But…
body: This app has been used my myself for many years now and is great! Just the initial download of maps is horribly s L o Wwww… I have checked my connection and that is robust, however I started to download maps for the USA last night and this morning I have a whopping 4 Megabytes of 2.3 Gig downloaded !!! At this rate it will take a week or two for the map to fully download! Sup with dat!?

title: I like the app but 2 things…
body: 1:) Could you add the speed limit to the map and also add how fast I’m going? Other apps offer this and it sure would be nice if you could offer this. 2:) Not sure it takes you the best route. I’m fairly certain it took me the long way to a destination I’m familiar with but also it doesn’t seem to factor in road work apparently.

title: Small inconvenience.
body: I like that I can choose my paths along the way and takes into consideration my height restrictions. My complaint was that I was not able to zoom out when I was trying to look further down the navigated path. We were trying to decide if we wanted to take a different way without cancelling the current path.

title: Great app...but..
body: We have been using this app for about 7 months (we are full timers that travel a lot) and have found it to be very reliable. However, we just sold our RV and purchased a new one. The new RV is 6” taller but the app is not allowing me to put in 13’ 5”. This makes us hesitant to use it because we would never want to get into an unsafe situation. I put a message into the developer so I’m hoping to get his taken care of quickly!

title: Great app
body: I like using this app for navigation, but paid for active traffic in April and have not received it.

title: Can use some improvements
body: Overall is a very good apps enough to make1 month purchased then 1 year purchased. what it lacks. 1- Needed Sound Alerts when approaching DOT Weight Stations, and able to adjustable distance incoming weight stations from 1 miles to 4 miles not lust little red icon “silence”. 2- Option to save your favorites Routes for future trip great tools for dedicated routes. 3- Incorporated live weather report, and warning in routes. 4- Live Truck stops with parkings and diesel prices. With these options would make Copilot the best apps

title: For me reliable
body: Overall I use this for my daily driving in conjunction with another GPS. My only problem it gives me is it puts off an exit and back on the same road, which is frustrating and a time waster. As far as hazmat routing and general routes I like it, I tend to use multiple stop feature for an entire trip. A big key is maps are downloaded to device instead of online. I would recommend this service, I wish the ETA’s were a little more accurate....

title: No CarPlay support
body: This app is fantastic in most ways. My two complaints are 1) this is not compatible with CarPlay so it doesn’t show up on my dashboard screen like Google Maps does. Instead I turn Google on with the volume muted and run Copilot on my phone with the volume on. This is sometimes confusing but much easier to glance at than the tiny phone screen. My other complaint is I can’t share saved trips across devices. They are saved as files locally to my device so I can’t open it on my wife’s phone for when she is driving. I have to duplicate the trip manually. For some reason Copilot rarely has truck stops by the brand and address shown on Google. This is usually okay to work around but I do find it odd.

title: Needs an update and soon
body: I love this app very much because I travel in an RV so I trust it’s not going to take me through a low overpass but it needs an update and real soon because I haven’t been able to use since last iPhone update. It just keeps crashing whenever I try to enter a destination. It wasn’t a cheap app either so it’s not fair that I haven’t been able to use it on my last two recent trips. I still give it four stars because when it works, it works! Update it please! UPDATE: Copilot finally contacted me and gave me clear and easy instructions to delete and reinstall the app and now it’s working like a charm again. Good customer service even though it’s a little slow.

title: Excellent GPS for commercial drivers and others!
body: I’ve been using CoPilot for quite a few years now (6+?) and have found it very reliable for guiding me to my destinations when operating heavy trucks. I previously had tried a few hardware/software packages from big names, like a Rand McNally tablet, and the CoPilot app simply blows them away! No special hardware needed as the app and its maps install on your phone and/or tablet! With the maps being stored on your device you needn’t have any concerns if you’re driving through a remote area where you have absolutely zero cell coverage! I know many truck drivers who just use Apple Maps or google maps and I’ve told all of them about CoPilot and how it can save your butt since it factors in the height, width, weight, and other factors of your rig (you can use one of multiple stock vehicle profiles or easily create one for your specific rig). If instead you run with a gps app meant for a commuter car then it will happily guide your 13’6” truck straight into a 10’ clearance rail bridge and you’ll be none the wiser until you’re wrecked or having to find a way to back up and turn around in traffic. Copilot only routes you on roads where you actually fit and where your vehicle is legal! You can even set it up to avoid mountains so you don’t find yourself driving in low-range 2nd gear at a crawl up on an interstate only to be later relying on your Jake brake and worn brake shoes to hold you back on a 8% down grade! Similarly you can tell the app which types of roads you prefer and which types you want to avoid. I absolutely recommend CoPilot to all professional drivers, and to others who have special routing/driving requirements! …don’t want to run your family RV under too short a clearance anymore than you would a mobile crane! If your career is behind a wheel then get this program, it’s not free but it is 100% worth every penny!

title: Best GPS app and always improving
body: If you depend on Apple Maps or Google Maps for navigation on Android or iPhone devices you’ll invariably find you don’t have cell service and your navigation is helpless, just when you really need it. CoPilot GPS has great maps of North America with periodic updates to stay current, and also supports RV routing profiles to avoid surprises of weight limited bridges and low overhead clearance. The routes are very stable once planned and not frequently trying to recalculate confusing alternates that are often useless and misleading which is a big complaint I have with Google. For the price and features nothing comes close to CoPilot GPS. The Facebook and twitter accounts don’t seem to be current or active at all, but that doesn’t matter, the app and data are well maintained.
